S34.01.note: The code shows a list of matching messages, not a jump to each match, so the Expected jump-between-matches part is not met in the code.
steps: Run agi, then send two or three messages that share one word.
Type /find <word> and press Return.

Look for a list of matches, each with a message number, a speaker (you or assistant) and a short snippet of the matching line, and compare with Expected. The code lists the matches; it does not jump the view to a message.
S34.01.where: In an open chat in the terminal app, type /find <text> and press Return

S34.02.needs: a few saved chats that contain a known word in a title or message
S34.02.note: The same search also runs inside a chat as /sessions search <query>, and the list is capped with a notice when there are many matches.
steps: Pick a word that appears in the title or a message of a saved chat.
Type agi --search <word> and press Return.
Look for the line "N session(s) matching" followed by the matching chats, and compare with Expected.
Open one match with agi --session <ID>, using an ID from the list, and check that the chat opens.
S34.02.where: In the terminal, type agi --search <query> and press Return

S34.06.needs: a paid account, a Managed Cloud chat, and Google Drive, Slack or Notion connected at the account's connectors page
S34.06.note: In Local or BYOK chats /connectors says the connectors are not offered, and on plans without the connectors capability it shows a refusal instead.
steps: Start a Managed Cloud chat with agi (not a Local or BYOK chat).
Type /connectors and press Return.
Read the line "Your account's connectors" and the note that Google Drive, Slack and Notion are offered to the chat.
Ask a question that needs a connected source, such as a file name in Drive, and check that an approval prompt appears before each connector call, then compare with Expected.
S34.06.where: In a Managed Cloud chat in the terminal app, type /connectors and press Return

labels.text: Usage: /search <question>, answer from a web search

S34.07.needs: a Brave Search or Tavily key for a Local or BYOK chat, or a Managed Cloud chat on a model that can search the web
S34.07.note: The search backends are the Brave and Tavily APIs, selected by environment variables or saved keys (apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/web/mod.rs).
steps: Start a chat with agi and make sure a Brave Search or Tavily key is saved, or use a Managed Cloud chat.
Type /search followed by a question about a current topic, and press Return.
Read the answer and look for a "Sources" block listing numbered titles and web addresses.
Compare the answer with the sources and with Expected.
S34.07.where: In a chat in the terminal app, type /search <question> and press Return

labels.text: Add a file to a project's knowledge, where its chats can search it.

S34.19.needs: a paid account with a project in it and a small text file to add
S34.19.note: Code found only adds files to a whole project; no control to pick one collection per chat or to limit a chat's search to it was found, so the choose-and-restrict part of Expected is not shown in the code.
steps: Type agi projects list and note a project name.
Type agi projects add-file "<project name>" <path to a small text file> and press Return.
Type agi projects show "<project name>" and look for the file under "Knowledge files", then compare with Expected.
S34.19.where: In the terminal, type agi projects add-file <project> <file> and press Return

S34.22.note: Only a general ask_user tool was found (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/tool_catalog.rs) that offers options for any question; nothing ties it to ambiguous search queries. Searched apps/cli/src for "clarif" only.

S34.27.note: The Sources block shows numbered titles and web addresses as plain text (apps/cli/src/sources.rs); searching apps/cli/src for open, xdg-open and webbrowser found no open-link action for sources.

labels.text: /search needs a web search key in this session.
Web search is not available on this account right now.

S34.32.needs: a chat with no search key saved for the first step; a Managed Cloud account whose plan blocks web search for the unavailable message
S34.32.note: The empty-result and provider-error messages are sent to the model, so the person sees only what the model writes about them, which the code does not guarantee.
steps: Start a Local or BYOK chat with no Brave Search or Tavily key saved, then type /search <question> and press Return.
Look for the message "/search needs a web search key in this session." and compare with Expected.
Type /search with a question made of nonsense words and check that the answer says the search found nothing, then compare with Expected.
S34.32.where: In a chat in the terminal app, type /search <question> and press Return
